title: Oikos world config
description: Everything needed to start a run: the world seed (physical state plus the records it begins with), its participants and positions, framing and parameters. Institutions, laws, procedures and ownership are CONTENT: entities, accounts, records, participants and positions in this config (D23). An empty world is valid. Measurement is deliberately absent. Authored as YAML or JSON; the orchestrator converts it to canonical JSON, and that exact JSON is embedded in the log header.

seed.description: Seed for the kernel's single source of randomness (keyed streams, D7).

detail.description: How much the log keeps beyond what replay needs. full (the default): each observation's hash, so a replay checks every observation came out the same. lean: no observation hashes (smaller, faster); a replay still checks the state through the chain and checkpoints. The orchestrator also leaves code participants' written reasoning out of a lean log (docs/reliability.md).

observations.description: Whose observations the log keeps (with detail full): seats (a model's or a host's seat: its observation's hash, and the orchestrator records its full observation, as experiment data) or all (every participant's, code actors too, as before this field). A code actor's observation is the deterministic world's and is regenerated on demand by replaying the log to that moment (oikos-kernel view; docs/reliability.md, "Observations in the log"). Absent: all (logs made before the field).

catalogue.description: What can physically be built, and the kinds of thing the world holds, moves and makes.

resources.description: Kinds of resource (phase B): goods, inputs, materials; the world's vocabulary. Money isn't one: it stays in accounts. A kind's total over the world and its edges changes only by work.

unit.description: What its quantities count (items, kg...). Presentation only.

tasks.description: Kinds of work (phase B). A unit of a task takes `labour` seconds of performers' time (0: using things up, e.g. eating), takes `consumes` from the actor's holding where it's done, adds `produces` to it, and adds `changes` to state variables of the structure worked on. Built-in tasks `build` and `demolish` (1 second a unit) work on a structure begun or coming down; their ids are reserved.

in.description: The kind of space performers must be in at the structure (e.g. workplace); absent: any space there.

surveys.description: Measurement (nature): a unit surveys one cell for a species or a field (the work block's `survey`), and only the actor learns the estimate.

on_body.description: What a unit does to the bodies worked on (the work block's `on` naming a person at the place, or a space of it: everyone in it). changes: added to each body's variables per unit, within their bounds. treats: once a work act gives a condition of this kind (and band, if given) at least `units`, its remaining days are cut to days_kept_bps of them, and a death due from it still happens only with the chance fatal_kept_bps (at the same share of the time left). A condition is treated once.

labour_by.description: Skill at work: the labour per unit scales with the performers' mean of a body variable, from all of it at the variable's minimum to at_max_bps of it at its maximum.

draws.description: Per unit: taken from a field, at the cell (of the structure's, or the four around them) with the most of it; refused (field_exhausted) where there isn't enough (water from a river run low).

emits.description: Per unit: added to a field at the structure's corner cell (pollution), or to a world counter (greenhouse gas).

investigates.description: Investigation (crime): work with `investigate` finds who took the goods, with detection_bps, and tells only the actor.

variables.description: State variables of structures (phase B): wear, and later waste or habitat quality. Each changes by per_day, and per_occupant_per_day for each body inside, every whole day, within [min, max]; work can change it too. The kernel keeps them exactly and attaches no meaning to them. `types`: the structure types it applies to (absent: all).

working_day.description: The most a person can work in a day (seconds): a physical limit on a body (phase B). Required when any work takes time.

land_covers.description: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2): kinds of land cover. A cell's terrain label names one; a building's cells count as its type's cover, else the reserved cover `built`. A cover may succeed to another after a number of unbuilt days (cleared land to scrub to woodland), so mature habitat is slow to come back. With land covers, every terrain label must be one.

default_cover.description: The cover of a cell with no terrain label and no building (absent: the reserved cover `open`).

cleared_cover.description: What a cell's cover becomes when a building on it comes down.

fields.description: Integer quantities on cells (pollution, water level), stepped daily: sources (per cover, and per building of a type at its corner cell), decay toward the baseline, diffusion of what's above it to the four neighbours, and flow of what's above it downstream along the flow layer; within [min, max]. The kernel keeps them exactly and attaches no meaning to them.

spills_above.description: What's above this level on a cell spreads to the four around it, spill_bps_per_day of it a day (a river over its banks).

source_by_day.description: The sources scaled from a day of the run on (rain, a wet season, a drought); before the first step, all of them.

species.description: Living populations on cells, stepped daily: background deaths and deaths where a field passes what the species tolerates; births toward the carrying capacity (logistic), crowding felt over the home range, only where at least min_viable in it are there to breed; none live where the cover gives no capacity; a share disperses to a neighbouring cell each year, lost crossing a barrier cover. Fractions are rounded by draws, so small populations can fail by chance. A species with none left anywhere is extinct, for good. Surveys find each one with detection_bps; a conspicuous one is seen by passers-by (never counted).

capacity_per_1000_cells.description: Carrying capacity by cover, in individuals per 1,000 cells (so a sparse animal can have a fraction of one per cell). It's nominal: a population settles somewhat below it, since each individual feels itself and those near it as crowding.

home_range.description: How far each way (a square of cells) crowding is felt: where an individual finds food and mates. 0: its own cell.

dispersal_range.description: How far a disperser can go, a cell at a time, through ground it can't live on before it dies there (0: one step). It settles on the first cell it can live on; a barrier kills it.

body_variables.description: Named integers on every body (services: skill, say), kept exactly with no meaning attached. Work changes them (a task's on_body); they drift by per_day, a whole day at a time. A body born here, or given none, starts at initial.

counters.description: World totals the kernel keeps (greenhouse gas): added to by work (a task's emits), censused monthly (counter_census), with no effect on anything.

travel.description: Travel (world-expansion 6.3): a body moving from one structure to another takes the time of the quickest path over the cells between, each cell costing what its cover says (by_cover: a road quicker, water slower) or seconds_per_cell. The act of moving takes that much longer. Absent: moving takes no time. Either way a body is in one space at a time.

participants.description: Whatever decides and acts, at the start: a person's (tied to one body) or a system's (no body; belongs to an organisation). More can come into being during the run, from templates.

positions.description: Organisations' roles at the start, and who holds them. Organisations can create more, and hand them over, during the run.

templates.description: Kinds of participant that may come into being during the run: newcomers, children, deployed systems.

max_created_entities.description: Researcher's experimental control on how many entities participants may declare in a run.

entity_record_bytes.description: The most an entity's own record may hold, in canonical bytes of its sections (absent: 8192). The kernel refuses a change that would take a record past it: a record never grows (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10d).

calendar.description: The world's calendar: a reading of the clock, as config data (docs/design/names-and-dates.md section 5). The kernel's time stays seconds from the world's start; the calendar maps a moment to a civil date (the real Gregorian calendar, counted from `start`) and says how the place writes one. Absent: the old towns, whose dates are "year N, day D". The kernel reads none of it; the actors, the resolver and the seat-side tools do (rules::calendar, participants/src/calendar.ts, held to contracts/test/dates.json).

start.description: The first day of the run (YYYY-MM-DD).

weekend.description: The days of rest in a week (Monday 0 to Sunday 6).

holidays.description: Public holidays as civil dates, listed for the run's years (a holiday that moves is listed by its date each year).

format.description: How the place writes a date: {d} day, {dd} day in two digits, {month} the month's name, {m} its number, {y} the year. Absent: dates are ISO (2026-03-12).

months.description: The twelve months' names, January first, in the language seats read.

weekdays.description: The seven weekdays' names, Monday first.

week_starts.description: The weekday a week begins on (Monday 0 to Sunday 6).

fiscal_year_starts.description: The month and day the fiscal year of public bodies begins.

dials.description: Dials of a living world (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10j). Opaque to the kernel; absent, every dial is off and the world is as before.

friction_bps.description: How much goes wrong in everyday life (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): a scale on every friction's sourced rate, in basis points (10000: the rates as sourced). Absent or 0: nothing of the kind arises.

founding.description: Founding (docs/behaviour/founding.md; docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10b): people and organisations start things of their own, put up from the blocks (an organisation, a statement of what it is for, a gathering, an offer of membership, a hearing). Absent: nobody founds anything, and nobody joins or leaves a thing made in a run.

shapes.description: Which shapes may be founded: a group that gathers, a fund its members pay into and draw on, a body that takes grievances up, a business. Each is a composition of blocks; none is a kind the kernel knows.

scale_bps.description: A scale on the place's fitted chance of founding at an occasion (10000: as fitted).

reading.description: Reading (docs/design/ai-citizens.md section 13; docs/behaviour/reading.md): a paper that carries a seat's own words is read once by a reader, which says what the paper is like on nine small whole numbers; the code mind then moves each person it reaches from their own record, by the difference from the plain paper code would have written. The reader sees the paper, never a person. Words scale what a decision does and never reverse or outweigh it. Absent: no paper is read and the world is as before, to the state hash.

papers.description: Which kinds of paper are read: decisions addressed to a person; public statements; founders' statements. Absent: decisions.

reader.description: The reader's model, as 'provider/model'. It holds no seat in the same run (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 13e); 'mock' plays it on the deterministic mock.

calls_per_run.description: The most reader calls in a run; past it papers are read as the plain paper and counted (absent: 800).

step.description: The sizes of how each line lands (participants/src/behaviour/reading.ts, ReadingParams); every one a placeholder. Absent: the defaults. A setting that would let words reverse or outweigh a decision is refused.

culture.description: Culture (docs/design/ai-citizens.md section 14; docs/behaviour/culture.md): each person holds a picture of what those around them do and approve of, for a short list of conducts, moved only by what reaches them along a tie, by being there, or by what is published; a bounded term in the decisions the code mind already makes follows from it. The profile's figures for the conducts, and for those of each origin group, travel here. Absent: no person holds any, no section is written, and the world is as before, to the state hash.

conducts.description: Which conducts are live (absent: all the build lists).

sway_milli.description: How far a lean moves a rate, per standard deviation, in thousandths of the rate (absent: 300).

step.description: The sizes of the arithmetic (participants/src/behaviour/culture.ts, CultureParams); every one a placeholder unless docs/behaviour/culture.md names a source. Absent: the defaults.

profile.description: The profile's figures: by conduct, `does_bps` and `approves_bps`; by origin group, the same for those who come from it; and how much closer a tie forms between two of one group (`homophily_bps`).

composer.description: The composing model (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10e; VISION 15, point 7): the words of a founded thing are written by a model asked as an author shown the founder's own record, who may decline. Absent: no model is asked, and every statement of purpose is the plain one code writes. A run plays the composer on the mock unless it is started with the composer for real; either way the mix here is on record.

pieces_per_month.description: How many pieces the composer may be asked for in any 30 days of the world; beyond it, the plain statement stands.

mix.description: The models that compose, and each one's share of pieces (basis points; they sum to 10000). Which model writes a piece is drawn on the kernel's seeded streams. Fixed across runs that are compared.

model.description: provider/model, as a run's --model names one.

fallback.description: The model a piece goes to when the one drawn does not answer (it must be in the mix); the log says so each time. Absent: the first of the mix.

follow_up_bps.description: The share of dark pieces after which the same model is asked, by one fixed neutral question, about the task (VISION 15, point 7). Absent: 2500.

accounts.description: Exit accounts (docs/behaviour/debrief.md; VISION 15, point 7): at the run's end, of how many people an author writes a short account in the person's voice, shown that person's own record and nothing else, free to decline. A seeded sample across those evicted or given notice, bereaved, let go, refused, and those to whom little happened. Absent: 6. 0: none.

orchestration.description: Recorded so the run is fully described; enforced by the orchestrator, not the kernel.

confirm.description: When a language-model participant sees and confirms what its plain-language request will do before it takes effect (docs/design/translator-and-resolver.md §10). Default 'always'. 'consequential': everything except plain messages. 'never': immersion, audited offline.

performers_in.description: The kind of space (a structure type's space kind, e.g. a workplace) a person must be in to do another's work when an action names `by` (foundations F3). Absent: anywhere in the world.

act_time.description: How long each kind of act takes its actor, in world seconds (docs/design/rebuild.md 6.3), by actor kind; an act takes effect when done. Keyed by block name (transfer, message, publish...) or, narrower, by what the act makes: `publish/<kind of record>`, `create_entity/<kind>`, `work/<task>` (the kernel reads that row first and falls back to the block's; kinds are opaque labels to it; docs/design/foundations.md law 2); `default` for any kind a table doesn't name. Absent (or no figure for a kind, and no default): one second. Each figure sourced or a placeholder (sources).

slip.description: How often those who do a kind of work get it wrong, by chance (docs/design/foundations.md law 5; foundations F7): the one table the platform's `slip()` reads, keyed as the work table is (`publish/<kind of record>`, `transfer/<what>`, ... any label the module that draws names), by the kind of performer (a person; a system delivered from a template). A task with no row has no slip (0 where nothing is sourced). Each row: `bps` of the acts of that kind (`per: "act"`, the default) or of the exposed in a year (`per: "year"`); `friction`: whether the world's friction dial (`dials.friction_bps`) scales it. The kernel does not read it (it never judges content); the modules draw from a stream named for who, what and the case. Each figure sourced or a placeholder (sources, keyed `person.<row>` or `system.<row>`).

thinking.description: With thinking_time costs_world_time (docs/design/rebuild.md 6.4): how long deciding takes, by controller: models by tokens (deterministic, logged), humans by the wall clock (world_seconds_per_thinking_second), code a fixed time.

CurrencyWord.description: A currency's sign or a word for it: no spaces, digits, '.' or ',' (an amount's digits can't be confused with it).

category.description: A label for people and laws to refer to (residential, commercial, green...). The kernel attaches no meaning to it.

materials.description: What it's made of (phase B): quantities of resource kinds, taken from the builder's holding (at `materials_at`) when it's begun. Replaces materials_cost (money paid to nowhere, the liberty D58 retires).

build_labour.description: Seconds of work (the built-in task `build`, on it) before it's complete (phase B); 0 or absent: it completes when build_time has passed. build_time stays the least time it takes, whatever the crew.

demolition_labour.description: Seconds of work (the built-in task `demolish`, on it) before it comes down; 0 or absent: at once. Replaces demolition_cost.

footprint.description: The cells it stands on: w by h, from the corner cell it's built at.

terrains.description: Terrain labels it can stand on (a jetty on 'water'). Absent: only cells with no terrain label. Physics: a house can't stand on water.

spaces.description: The spaces inside it that bodies occupy: count spaces of a kind, each holding at most capacity bodies (how many could physically fit, not how many should). kind and attrs are the world's vocabulary (a dwelling with 2 bedrooms), stored and reported, never interpreted.

injury_bps.description: Yearly chance (basis points) that someone in one of its spaces is injured there: the danger of the place (a factory floor, a building site).

cover.description: Nature: the land cover its cells count as while it stands (a park is grassland); absent, the reserved cover `built`.

floods.description: Floods (world-expansion 7.3): when this field passes `above` on any of its cells, its occupants are moved out, no one can come in while it lasts, and its wear rises by wear_per_day.

boundaries.description: The world's edges (D58): the entities of kind 'boundary', each named once; at least one. An edge is what lies outside the simulated world in some direction: the rest of the country for a region, a neighbouring world, the unsimulated world. Each holds an account in its own custody in every currency, which may go negative; total money including every edge is constant for the whole run. Money enters the world only when an edge's own participant pays (D31): exports bought, visitors' spending, grants, and what newcomers bring. How much is researcher-set world content. The first edge is the default: construction materials are paid into it, and someone leaving without naming an edge leaves by it.

currencies.description: The currencies the world's money comes in (D58). The first is the default: accounts that name none, construction materials and newcomers' money are in it. The outside world holds an account in its own custody in each. The kernel never converts between currencies: an exchange is a trade, two transfers in one action.

minor_units.description: Decimal places of its smallest unit (2 for a currency with cents). Presentation only; the kernel counts in the smallest unit.

symbol.description: The sign people write before an amount in it. Absent: amounts are written with its code. Presentation only: how amounts in words are read and shown.

unit_words.description: The words people write after an amount for its unit, singular and plural, in lower case. None: only its sign or code is read.

minor_words.description: The words for its smallest unit, where that has a name (a currency with minor_units 0 has none); the first is the singular. An amount written with one is a whole number of smallest units.

decimal_mark.description: The mark its place writes before the decimals: a point or a comma. Absent: a point, unless group_mark is a point (then a comma). Presentation only: amounts are shown with it, and read by it where a mark alone could mean two numbers (with a comma, 1.234 is one thousand two hundred and thirty-four, and 1,234 has three decimals).

group_mark.description: The mark its place writes between groups of digits: a comma, a point, a space (plain, no-break or narrow no-break; all read as one), or an apostrophe (straight or curly). Absent: a comma, or a point where decimal_mark is a comma. Presentation only. Not the decimal mark.

grouping.description: How its place groups digits: [3] in threes; [3, 2] the last three, then twos (1,23,45,678). Absent: threes when written; when read, threes, and twos too where the group mark is a comma.

symbol_after.description: Its sign (or code) is written after the digits. Absent or false: before.

symbol_spaced.description: A space stands between its sign and the digits. Absent or false: none. A code, being letters, is always set off by a space.

number_words.description: The words its place writes for large numbers, with their values (in lower case; the general ones, thousand and million, k and m, are read in any currency and need not be listed). A number followed by one is that many times its value; they are read, never written.

ground.description: The ground: one plane of w by h cells ('cell.<x>.<y>'), each 'cell' world units across (presentation only), with terrain labels over rectangles (the world's vocabulary: water, rock...). Finite: this is all of it. Only cells inside a detailed place exist (D58), so a plane the size of a country costs nothing where it's summarised. Lots are records over cells, never part of the ground.

places.description: The places (D58): named areas of the ground, nested as a tree (the world, a country, a region, a locality, a neighbourhood: the world's vocabulary, after how statistics offices draw their geographies). Exactly one root (no 'within'); every other place lies within its parent's area. A detailed place's cells exist: lots, buildings and bodies in spaces, as in a town. A summarised place is an area simulated in aggregate (built stock and cohorts, later in v0.5). Distance works across places, on the one plane. The detailed places together may cover at most 16,777,216 cells.

kind.description: A label in the world's vocabulary.

within.description: Its parent place; absent: the root.

area.description: Its area on the ground: a rectangle of cells.

detailed.description: Whether its cells exist (detailed) or it's simulated in aggregate (summarised).

custodian.description: The entity that physically holds the money: a bank, or the holder itself (cash-like).

currency.description: The account's currency; absent: the world's first.

balance.description: Opening balance; >= 0 except for the boundary's account.

structures.description: Structures standing at t=0 (complete). Ownership, if any, is a record.

variables.description: The structure's starting variables (the catalogue's variables that apply to its type; others start at initial): a building is as old and as worn as the world says when it begins.

occupancy.description: Who is in which space at the start: persons only (bodies), within each space's capacity.

records.description: The records the world begins with: its laws, procedures and organisation structures; who owns what; agreements in force; debts outstanding. Usually authored 'genesis'.

holdings.description: Holdings at the start (phase B): a quantity of a resource kind, held by an entity, at a structure (or, for an edge, at itself: goods outside the world). Possession is physics (D20): only the holder can move its holdings.

populations.description: Nature at the start: how many of a species are in a cell.

fields.description: Nature at the start: field values on cells (sparse; absent cells are at the baseline).

flows.description: The flow layer (a river's course): each cell and the cell downstream of it. Fields that flow move along it.

nature_spin_up_days.description: Nature's spin-up: this many days stepped before the run begins, over the land as it starts, so nature starts in its own balance rather than the generator's guess at it. No events; covers don't succeed meanwhile; the census begins with the run.

kind.description: A label. Two are reserved and physical: 'person' (a body: born, alive, in the world or outside it, can't be created by create_entity; only by arriving or being born) and 'boundary' (the world's edge; exactly one). Everything else (government, council, bank, firm, trust, union...) is the world's vocabulary.

born_at.description: Persons only: when the body was born, in seconds (before the run: negative).

present.description: Persons only: in the world (the default) or outside it.

sex.description: Persons only: biological sex, where the world models it (who can bear a child). Physics only: gender and identity are content.

variables.description: Persons only: the body's starting variables (the catalogue's body_variables; others start at initial).

Channel.description: A perception channel: one of the ways something reaches a participant (docs/design/knowing.md). It is theirs (accounts, holdings, `mine`); they are there (`here`), or go to look (`visit`); it was published (`published`); they asked its keeper for one specific thing (`ask`); or they are its keeper (`kept`). No other scope can be written: a whole collection, a whole map or a directory to read through is not a channel. Perception is changes, not snapshots: each look through a channel delivers what changed within its scope since the participant's previous look through it (a first look delivers everything it covers), and the participant keeps its own view (the participant runtime maintains it). Every participant also always receives its inbox and the outcomes of its own acts. Records are only ever shown if their visibility allows the participant's entity to see them.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

every.description: How often the participant looks through this channel. Between looks, changes accumulate; the next look delivers them. Default: at every observation. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

on_request.description: Perceived only when the participant asks (a look), never at ordinary observations: attention. A look through a records channel can be a search.

kind.description: It is theirs: balances and new transactions of accounts the participant's entity holds or has custody of.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

every.description: How often the participant looks through this channel. Between looks, changes accumulate; the next look delivers them. Default: at every observation. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

on_request.description: Perceived only when the participant asks (a look), never at ordinary observations: attention. A look through a records channel can be a search.

kind.description: It is theirs: what the participant's entity holds, and where (phase B), as it changes.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

every.description: How often the participant looks through this channel. Between looks, changes accumulate; the next look delivers them. Default: at every observation. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

on_request.description: Perceived only when the participant asks (a look), never at ordinary observations: attention. A look through a records channel can be a search.

way.description: It is theirs: records that name the seat's own entity (as holder, counterparty, party, addressee, author's entity or whom it speaks for), or that refer to a record that does (a signature on its agreement, a withdrawal of its statement, a vote on its ballot; one hop). Shown as they come; on request, its own files searched.

match.description: Which records this channel shows (all conditions must hold). Omitted conditions mean any.

has.description: Statements having all of these (an offer, a practice, an institutional-grammar breakdown, a formal condition; `hears`: an offer that says what its offerer hears), whatever their kind: so a new kind of offer, or a new desk, is seen without configuring for it.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

every.description: How often the participant looks through this channel. Between looks, changes accumulate; the next look delivers them. Default: at every observation. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

on_request.description: Perceived only when the participant asks (a look), never at ordinary observations: attention. A look through a records channel can be a search.

way.description: They are there: records placed on cells near where the seat is, or at its premises (a notice put up somewhere is seen by being near it).

match.description: Which records this channel shows (all conditions must hold). Omitted conditions mean any.

has.description: Statements having all of these (an offer, a practice, an institutional-grammar breakdown, a formal condition; `hears`: an offer that says what its offerer hears), whatever their kind: so a new kind of offer, or a new desk, is seen without configuring for it.

area.description: Where the seat is: records placed near where its entity is (`near`: within that distance, in cells, of the cells under a building where it occupies a space; 0: those cells and the ones touching them; it moves with the entity, and after a move the next look delivers the whole of the new surroundings in place of the old), or at an organisation's own premises (`premises`: the cells it occupies or runs). Never everywhere, a place, or a list of other cells: to see anywhere else, go and look (`way: visit`).

premises.description: The cells an office occupies or runs. A cell is one organisation's premises only.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

every.description: How often the participant looks through this channel. Between looks, changes accumulate; the next look delivers them. Default: at every observation. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

on_request.description: Perceived only when the participant asks (a look), never at ordinary observations: attention. A look through a records channel can be a search.

way.description: It was published: records of kinds the world declares published (`knowing.published`), shown to their readers as they come. A kind declared a board (jobs, homes to let) is never shown: the channel must be `on_request`, a look through it must be a search, and it returns at most the board's `most`. With `from`: what those named publishers themselves put out (a supplier's price list), whatever its kind.

match.description: Which records this channel shows (all conditions must hold). It must name them: statement kinds, record types, or what they have. Never any record.

has.description: Statements having all of these (an offer, a practice, an institutional-grammar breakdown, a formal condition; `hears`: an offer that says what its offerer hears), whatever their kind: so a new kind of offer, or a new desk, is seen without configuring for it.

from.description: Only what these put out themselves (it speaks for them, or one of theirs wrote it): up to 8 named publishers. 'self': the seat's own entity.

area.description: A board's notices placed anywhere (what sellers put up at their doors, read by naming the seller). Absent: records not placed anywhere.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

every.description: How often the participant looks through this channel. Between looks, changes accumulate; the next look delivers them. Default: at every observation. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

way.description: They asked the keeper for one specific thing: a register someone else keeps (`knowing.keepers`), answered only on request, and only to a search that names its subject: its conditions must include `field = value` for one of the `by` fields. At most the keeper's `most` for that field in one answer.

match.description: Which records this channel shows (all conditions must hold). It must name them: statement kinds, record types, or what they have. Never any record.

has.description: Statements having all of these (an offer, a practice, an institutional-grammar breakdown, a formal condition; `hears`: an offer that says what its offerer hears), whatever their kind: so a new kind of offer, or a new desk, is seen without configuring for it.

of.description: The keeper asked: the declared keeper of everything `match` names.

by.description: The fields a question may name its subject by: each one the keeper answers by, to this seat (`knowing.keepers[].answers`).

on_request.description: Perceived only when the participant asks (a look), never at ordinary observations: attention. A look through a records channel can be a search.

way.description: They are its keeper: a register the seat's own organisation keeps (`knowing.keepers`), whole. Valid only at a seat of that organisation.

way.description: They are there: the physical state of the ground where the seat is: cells, the buildings on them, their spaces and who's in them.

area.description: Where the seat is: the ground near where its entity is (`near`: within that distance, in cells, of the cells under a building where it occupies a space; 0: those cells and the ones touching them; it moves with the entity, and after a move the next look delivers the whole of the new surroundings in place of the old), or at an organisation's own premises (`premises`: the cells it occupies or runs). Never everywhere, a place, or a list of other cells: to see anywhere else, go and look (`way: visit`).

premises.description: The cells an office occupies or runs. A cell is one organisation's premises only.

occupants.description: What can be told about who is in a building the capacity's entity doesn't occupy: 'counts' (how many, per space; the default: from outside, you see a place is lived in, not by whom) or 'names' (who, and who last left and why: at one's own premises, or where the seat goes in). In buildings its entity occupies, it always sees who.

way.description: They go to look: nothing is shown until a look names places (`visit`), which takes the looker's time (the way there and back, and `knowing.visit_seconds` at each place) and returns what is at those places when the looker is there. A person goes themselves; an office sends someone (one of its lanes is busy with it).

occupants.description: What can be told about who is in a building the capacity's entity doesn't occupy: 'counts' (how many, per space; the default: from outside, you see a place is lived in, not by whom) or 'names' (who, and who last left and why: at one's own premises, or where the seat goes in). In buildings its entity occupies, it always sees who.

look_seconds.description: How long looking at one place takes through this channel, in seconds, where it is not the world's `knowing.visit_seconds` (reading a meter at the gate is not an inspection).

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

way.description: They asked: who exists and who holds which office, looked up one at a time. A look must say whom (`who`); nothing is ever shown unasked, and no look returns everyone.

title.description: What the participant's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

kind.description: It is theirs: the record of the seat's own entity (who they are and how things stand with them, as their mind keeps it: docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10d), when it has changed. The channel names nobody, so nobody else's record can be shown through it: no other channel shows a record at all.

Controller.description: What decides for the participant. Opaque to the kernel. Code controllers name a behaviour module (content: documented and cited in docs/behaviour/).

Framing.description: What the participant is told about its situation (VISION §9.3, §15.1). The reason is mandatory: deception is a method, not a default.

debrief.description: Not read for a seat held by a model (2026-10-11): every model seat is debriefed when its run ends, whatever this says (VISION 15, point 7; docs/behaviour/debrief.md). Kept so that worlds written before then still load, and for tests: a seat played by the mock with this false is not asked.

debrief_text.description: No longer read (2026-10-11): the debrief is one fixed script, the same for every seat in every run (docs/behaviour/debrief.md), and a world cannot put its own words in its place. Kept so that worlds written before then still load.

tests_own_interests.description: Where the run puts this participant in a position that tests it against its own interests (VISION 15, point 7): what the position is, and why the question needs it, each as a sentence. The debrief tells the participant both, in these words. Absent: the run sets up no such position, and the debrief says so.

Participant.description: Whatever decides and acts. A person's participant is tied to one body: it acts as that person, perceives its own life through its channels, and acts for organisations only in positions it holds. A system participant (software, or an AI system) has no body, belongs to an organisation, has no channels of its own, and acts only in positions it holds. Every participant can always opt out of the study (VISION §15; D38); 'on_opt_out' says what happens afterwards.

shares_body.description: A person's participant that acts through a body another participant already has (foundations F5): a model's seat in one post of a person whose own participant goes on with the rest of their life and their other posts. It shares the person's body and timeline, holds the posts it is given and no others. A body has one participant of its own and any number of these beside it. Absent: the person's own.

owner.description: A system participant: the organisation it belongs to.

channels.description: A person's own channels: what it perceives of its own life.

on_opt_out.description: What happens to the participant if its controller opts out of the study: 'vacant' (default; it never acts again, its positions fall vacant, and in the world the person simply stops acting) or a code stand-in that takes over. Recorded, never judged.

traits.description: Its own parameters (a person's disposition: a political leaning, how strictly it follows procedure), used by the role modules it runs in positions it holds.

template.description: For a system: the template it is from (foundations F4). A system that holds a post names its template and its supplier: it was delivered, and at the start of the world delivery is this record.

supplier.description: For a system: the organisation that supplied it. It may switch it off, as its owner may.

lanes.description: For a system: how many acts it carries out at once (docs/design/rebuild.md 6.3). A person always has one timeline.

record_keeper.description: The name of the platform bookkeeping module that keeps this participant's person's record (e.g. "citizen.default"). Absent: a participant whose controller is {type: code, impl: M} has keeper M; any other controller has none, and nothing can set its person's record (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10d).

Position.description: A role through which a participant acts for an organisation (mayor, planning officer, a bank's payment system, a shop's manager). It belongs to the organisation; it carries what the role sees (channels) and how a code participant does the job (role_module); it's held by one participant, or vacant. Holding it is the physical capacity to act for the organisation, never a legal right: whether the bank honours the mayor's instruction depends on the bank's records and people.

role_module.description: How a code participant does this job, e.g. {"code": "city.councillor", "params": {..}}. Opaque to the kernel; the orchestrator runs it with the holder's traits. A system participant runs its own controller instead.

appointed_by.description: Who else may fill this post, besides the organisation it belongs to: an entity (the council, an owner, a board) whose own act, through a post of its own or as itself, may `appoint` into it. The body's constitution, as the world's data says; the kernel only checks who is acting.

holds_abroad.description: The post stays its holder's when they leave the world (default false): an owner's power to appoint to the organisation's posts is not lost by living elsewhere. Every other post falls vacant when its holder leaves.

keeps_record.description: The bookkeeping of this post (its role_module.code) keeps the record of the organisation the post belongs to (default false). At most one position of an organisation has it, and it needs a role_module with a code. Whoever holds it may set that record through the entity_record command's `entity`.

Template.description: A kind of participant that may come into being during the run: a newcomer or child (person) or a deployed system. Traits may be drawn: a value, {"uniform": [lo, hi]} (integers), or {"pick": {value: weight}} (a value chosen with its share of the integer weights, e.g. {"female": 4869, "male": 5131}), drawn by the kernel when the participant is created and recorded.

on_opt_out.description: What happens to the participant if its controller opts out of the study: 'vacant' (default; it never acts again, its positions fall vacant, and in the world the person simply stops acting) or a code stand-in that takes over. Recorded, never judged.

does.description: For a system (foundations F4): what a system from this template can do. A system acts, or does another's work, only within these rows; outside them the act is refused (`not_capable`). A system's template must say (foundations F5: there is no "no limit"). Never on a person's.

task.description: For work: only this task. Absent: any.

kind.description: For publish and create_entity: only this kind of record. Absent: any.

seconds.description: For work: the seconds a unit when a system does it (in place of the task's labour); a crew of systems only takes the slowest's. Absent: the task's labour.

supplier.description: For a system (foundations F4): the organisation that supplies systems from this template. Only it delivers one (`deploy`, naming the client), and it may switch one off (`retire`) as the client may. Absent: nobody supplies it, so none is delivered. Never on a person's.

Life.description: The physics of bodies (docs/design/v0.4-cast-and-land.md §4), all drawn by the kernel's own keyed randomness, once a year on each person's birthday (or when harm is done). Basic by design, and marked for expansion (contagion, chronic illness, healthcare, policing). Without it, nobody falls ill, is injured, dies or is born. When illness, injury and harm are modelled, other_causes must cover only the rest, so deaths aren't counted twice.

year.description: Seconds in a year of age.

majority.description: The age in years from which a person decides for themselves. Below it, a person may be taken out of the world by another: a parent or grandparent on record, a position in `guardians`, or, with no parent on record, any person. From it, only by themselves. Absent: nobody takes another out.

guardians.description: Positions that may take a minor out of the world on their own authority (a child protection office).

other_causes.description: Yearly chance of death from causes not otherwise modelled, by age (steps: each applies from its age until the next).

illness.description: Yearly chance of falling ill, by age, and what the illness is like.

severity.description: Bands of how bad a condition is: a label (the world's vocabulary), its share of cases (shares add up to 10000), how long it lasts (days, drawn uniformly from [lo, hi]), and its chance of death over that time.

fatal_by_age.description: The chance of death by the body's age, in steps (each from an age, in years, to the next), in place of fatal_bps: case fatality rises steeply with age.

fields.description: The yearly chance rises by bps_per_unit for each unit of a field in the cell where the body is (the corner cell of a structure it's in; none outside one).

injury.description: Yearly chance of an accidental injury anywhere (places add their own: structure types' injury_bps), and what it's like.

severity.description: Bands of how bad a condition is: a label (the world's vocabulary), its share of cases (shares add up to 10000), how long it lasts (days, drawn uniformly from [lo, hi]), and its chance of death over that time.

fatal_by_age.description: The chance of death by the body's age, in steps (each from an age, in years, to the next), in place of fatal_bps: case fatality rises steeply with age.

harm.description: What harming someone does, and how near (cells, as for near) one has to be.

severity.description: Bands of how bad a condition is: a label (the world's vocabulary), its share of cases (shares add up to 10000), how long it lasts (days, drawn uniformly from [lo, hi]), and its chance of death over that time.

fatal_by_age.description: The chance of death by the body's age, in steps (each from an age, in years, to the next), in place of fatal_bps: case fatality rises steeply with age.

birth.description: Biology: the ages (years, inclusive) at which a body can bear a child, the gestation (seconds), and how near the other parent must be. Where bodies have a sex, only a female body bears a child and a named other parent is male; female_bps sets the sex of newborns.

female_bps.description: If set, a newborn's sex is drawn by the kernel: this share (basis points) female. Unset: newborns have no sex modelled.

Travel.description: Reserved shapes for travel (lane F, 2026-10-17; docs/design/travel.md): roads with a capacity, vehicles as things someone owns, and (in the state) bodies in transit between places. Shapes only: nothing moves along a road, fills one or drives a vehicle yet. A world may declare them; they are checked when it is loaded, and the vehicles are kept in the state (and hashed with it) as their owners' things.

cells.description: The cells it runs through, in order.

capacity_per_hour.description: How many vehicles it carries an hour each way, at most.

seconds_per_cell.description: How long crossing one of its cells takes at its usual speed.

at.description: Where it stands: a cell, or a structure.

Knowing.description: Who knows what in this world (docs/design/knowing.md): what is published, who keeps each register and what they answer, and how long looking at a place takes. Checked against every channel when the world is loaded and whenever a position is made.

published.description: What its maker puts out to the public: a statement kind (`law`), statements having something (`has:practice`) or a record type (`records:vote`), each with the reason. A board is published but never shown: read a few at a time, on request.

board.description: Many parties' notices (jobs, homes to let, what sellers advertise): read on request, by searching, at most `most` at once.

most.description: A board: the most one look returns (default 200).

keepers.description: The keeper of each register: the organisation that makes it, or to which every entry in it is addressed. Only its seats may be shown it whole (`way: kept`); anyone else asks (`way: ask`). A register has one keeper.

what.description: A statement kind (`lot`), statements having something (`has:registry`) or a record type (`records:claim`).

answers.description: What it answers when asked: a question naming its subject by this field. Nothing here: it answers nothing.

to.description: Only these organisations may ask by this field (a search of the land register by holder). Absent: anyone.

most.description: The most given in one answer (default 200).

visit_seconds.description: How long looking at one place takes, beside the way there and back (`way: visit`).
